papers.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties II. Fibrations over a polarized base
papers.abstract: We extend the height and energy inequalities for fibrations over curves to a fibration $f:X\to Y$ over a polarized variety $(Y,B)$. For an integrable relatively nef adelic line bundle $\bar L$, we prove a height inequality under the assumption that $L$ is nef on the inverse image of a geometric generic complete-intersection curve in $Y$. We deduce a lower bound for the local energy at almost every complex or nonarchimedean realization of a fixed polarized model when $L$ is $f$-ample. For a slope semistable bundle on a fixed polarized complex variety, we show that the infimum of the energy on its projective bundle equals the infimum of Donaldson's functional on Hermitian quotient metrics, with the normalization given below.

papers.title: Rotationally symmetric fractional minimal surfaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide a non-trivial example of an $s$-minimal surface that is invariant under rotations. More precisely, we study alternating radial sets whose boundaries are finite or locally finite unions of concentric spheres and prove that, fixing the outer radius to $r=1$, there exists a radial configuration for which the fractional mean curvature $H_s$ vanishes at every free interface. We then show that rescaling radial maximizers by their innermost radius and passing to the limit yields a properly embedded, rotationally symmetric, locally finite hypersurface satisfying $H_s=0$ at every point of the boundary.

papers.title: Equivariant harmonic maps from $\mathbb{S}^3$ to $\mathbb{S}^2$: on a counterexample to a conjecture of J. Eells
papers.abstract: The present paper builds on a remarkable AI-generated counterexample to a long-standing conjecture of James Eells. We present the rigorous construction of a smooth harmonic map $f:\mathbb{S}^3\to \mathbb{S}^2$ between the round spheres which does not factor through a Hopf fibration, and improve some arguments to get that the Hopf invariant of $f$ is either $0$ or $\pm 6$. The construction is based on a min-max scheme in a $5$-equivariant class of maps $f$ with an additional dihedral symmetry. By passing to a suitable associated sphere bundle over $\mathbb{S}^2$, the problem is reduced to a variational problem for sections, where the imposed symmetries guarantee the mountain pass structure and the non-constancy of the desired limit harmonic map.

papers.title: Ancient solutions of mean curvature flow in a slab
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study complete ancient solutions of the mean curvature flow in arbitrary codimension contained in slabs in Euclidean space. Under a natural principal-angle condition, we prove that a translating soliton contained in a slab of width less than $\pi$ cannot be bounded from below in the translating direction, and characterize the grim reaper cylinder in form of a rigidity result at the critical width $\pi$. We derive corresponding results for ancient solutions confined in slabs.

papers.title: The Minimal Background Period for Infinitely Many Spectral Gaps in Anderson-Bernoulli Models
papers.abstract: We consider one-dimensional discrete Schr\"odinger operators with a periodic background and independent Bernoulli disorder. We ask for the least background period permitting infinitely many gaps in the almost sure spectrum. We provide explicit rational parameters at the minimum period of three, answering Wood's question. Our example gives negative answers to Bellissard's question for a disconnected background hull and to Damanik and Fillman's two finite-gap questions for transitive subshifts of finite type and subshifts of positive entropy. The proof, which appears to be new, normalizes the first background value to zero and establishes a transverse heteroclinic connection at nonzero energy. A strict scale window yields invariant multicones. For every nondegenerate Bernoulli law, gaps accumulate from the right at this spectral point. This accumulation persists under small perturbations, with its energy varying real analytically. Spectral intervals approach this point from the right, ruling out a Cantor spectrum. Three is the least background period at which exact recovery of the spectrum from periodic realizations can require unbounded fundamental periods of the total potential.

papers.title: Mass equidistribution and fluctuations for random holomorphic sections of big line bundles with continuous metrics
papers.abstract: We study mass equidistribution and fluctuations of random holomorphic sections of big line bundles over compact complex manifolds, equipped with continuous Hermitian metrics and Bernstein-Markov measures. For arrays of centered coefficients that are independent and identically distributed within each row, we establish sharp moment conditions for mass equidistribution, covering a broad class of distributions, including Gaussian and certain discrete laws. On compact K\"ahler manifolds, we also show that mass equidistribution implies equidistribution of zeros under a natural condition on the equilibrium measure. We further establish central limit theorems beyond the Gaussian setting, show that fluctuations may depend on the choice of orthonormal basis, and determine their limiting variances for Haar-almost every sequence of bases.

papers.title: Sub-Riemannian Distances on Lie Groups: Tangent Asymptotics and Hermitian Matrix Formulas
papers.abstract: Let $d_{\mathrm{SR}}$ be the Carnot--Carath\'{e}odory distance associated with a two-step Lie pair and let $d_0$ be the distance on its nilpotent tangent group. For compact Lie pairs we prove, locally uniformly in $(X,Z)$, \[ d_{\mathrm{SR}}\!\left(e,\exp(rX+r^2Z)\right)^2 =r^2d_0(e,(X,Z))^2+O(r^3). \] For symmetric pairs, the remainder improves to $O(r^4)$. This order is sharp in general, and the estimate remains uniform at cut points, abnormal endpoints, and points where the tangent endpoint map changes rank. If the tangent minimizer is unique, the endpoint differential is onto, and the constrained Hessian is coercive, we determine the coefficient of $r^4$ with remainder $O(r^6)$. For block subgroups of $\mathrm{SU}(N)$, we express the vertical squared distance on the tangent group as the attained minimum of a finite-dimensional functional on Hermitian matrices subject to linear constraints on their partial traces. Every minimizer gives a minimizing loop represented by a trigonometric polynomial. For one $m$-dimensional block and $q$ scalar blocks, the coefficient has weights $\lceil j/q\rceil$ and reduces to a trace norm formula when $q\ge\lfloor m/2\rfloor$.

papers.title: Uniqueness Results for Static Asymptotically Locally Hyperbolic (ALH) Manifolds
papers.abstract: We give uniqueness results for related classes of static asymptotically locally hyperbolic (ALH) manifolds. As an application, we give examples of one ended hyperbolic manifolds with boundary that are not optimal for the Positive Mass Theorem or for the Riemannian Penrose Inequality

papers.title: Convergence rate of rescaled mean curvature flows over asymptotically conical shrinkers
papers.abstract: We study how rapidly a rescaled mean curvature flow can approach an asymptotically conical self-shrinker. For a global normal graph with small $C^1$ norm and time-integrable $C^0$ norm, we prove that every nonzero solution has a leading asymptotic term given by an eigenfunction of the linearized operator $L$. In particular, a global graph $u$ with $e^{kt}\|u\|_{C^1}\to 0$ for every $k$ must coincide with the shrinker. We also construct a nonzero local graph over an immersed asymptotically conical shrinker with $C^2$ super-exponential decay in every bounded subset. This flow is defined on expanding open graphical domains. The example illustrates how rigidity fails in the local graphical setting.

papers.title: On the existence of PMC hypersurfaces in complete manifolds of finite volume
papers.abstract: Let $M^{n+1}$, $n+1\geq 3$, be a complete Riemannian manifold of finite volume, and suppose that $h\in C^{\infty}(M) \cap L^1(M)$ has the property that the width of $M$ \wrt\ the $\mathcal{A}^h$ functional, $W^h(M)$, is positive. Then there exists a hypersurface $\Sigma \subset M$ with prescribed mean curvature $h$, satisfying $0<\mathcal{H}^n(\Sigma)<\infty$. Furthermore, $\Sigma$ is a closed subset of $M$ and it is smooth and almost embedded outside a singular set of Hausdorff dimension $\leq n-7$. The condition $W^h(M)>0$ is satisfied if $\|h\|_{L^1(M)}< W(M)$ (where $W(M)$ is the width of $M$ with respect to the area functional) or $\|h\|_{L^\infty(M)}< [\mathscr{I}]_0$ (where $\mathscr{I}$ is the isoperimetric profile of $M$ and $[\mathscr{I}]_0:=\sup_{v>0} \frac{\mathscr{I}(v)}{v}$).

papers.title: A Sharp Lower Bound for the First Nonzero Steklov Eigenvalue of the Witten Laplacian on Weighted Surfaces with Nonnegative Bakry-Emery-Ricci Tensor
papers.abstract: We consider compact connected weighted surfaces with smooth boundary whose Bakry-Emery-Ricci tensor is nonnegative. We assume that the geodesic curvature of the boundary is bounded below in terms of the normal and tangential derivatives of the weight function. Under these assumptions, we prove a lower bound for the first nonzero Steklov eigenvalue of the Witten Laplacian, which is sharp in the sense that equality holds if and only if the surface is isometric to a Euclidean disk and the weight function is constant.

papers.title: Contractible 4-Manifolds with Nonnegative Ricci Curvature and Euclidean Volume Growth
papers.abstract: We prove that every contractible smooth 4-manifold admitting a complete Riemannian metric with nonnegative Ricci curvature and Euclidean volume growth is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^4$. More precisely, every compact subset lies in the interior of a connected compact regular domain with simply connected complement. The key construction produces compact domains whose boundaries admit positive scalar curvature and which are regular sublevels of global strictly three-convex Morse exhaustions. A topological criterion forces the exterior fundamental group to be trivial whenever it contains no nonabelian free subgroup and satisfies the resulting boundary, homological, and relative cell hypotheses; in the geometric application, this group is finite. Its proof uses a cellular formulation of the Gerstenhaber-Rothaus theorem and a smooth filling obstruction. The resulting complements give simple connectivity at infinity, and Freedman's recognition theorem completes the argument.

papers.title: Harmonic multi-valued $1$-forms and deformations of branched covers of special Lagrangians
papers.abstract: This article introduces the notion of a non-degenerate multi-valued $1$-form on a manifold $X$ in terms of immersed submanifolds of $T^*X$ and develops a deformation theory extending Donaldson's work on harmonic non-degenerate $\mathbf{Z}/2\mathbf{Z}$ $1$-forms. More precisely, the universal moduli space of harmonic non-degenerate multi-valued $1$-forms is shown to be a tame Fr\'echet orbifold whose projection onto the space of Riemannian metrics is a submersion and whose fibres are locally parametrised by their periods. The proof relies on H\"ormander's subelliptic estimates and the Nash--Moser submersion theorem. As an application of this analytic framework, harmonic multi-valued $1$-forms on a special Lagrangian are shown to control deformations of its branched covers, extending work of He for multiplicity two.

papers.title: Area-minimizing surfaces and the rigidity of three-dimensional electrostatic systems
papers.abstract: We study three-dimensional electrostatic systems, the Riemannian data of static solutions of the Einstein--Maxwell equations with cosmological constant $\Lambda$, by means of locally area-minimizing surfaces. Such a surface with non-empty boundary on the horizons is a totally geodesic hemisphere and forces the de Sitter system. A closed one in the interior forces a system of product type, one of eight models if the scalar curvature is somewhere positive on it, among them the Bertotti--Robinson, Nariai and cold and ultracold black hole systems. No compactness, asymptotic or pinching assumption is needed. In particular, closed systems without horizons are flat or compact quotients of the Nariai--Bertotti--Robinson system. For compact systems with connected horizon, the electric field vanishes even when the system is not simply connected, and the area of the horizon is either $12\pi/\Lambda$, for de Sitter, or at most $4\pi/\Lambda$. With several horizons, every horizon whose area does not exceed the sum of the others is stable, minimizes area in its homology class and satisfies an area--charge inequality, with equality only for the charged Nariai systems; its charged Hawking mass and charge therefore lie in the parameter region of the Reissner--Nordstr\"om--de Sitter black holes. Compact systems with horizons are spherical space forms with balls removed. Noncompact systems with strictly mean-convex ends have one end, and their horizons are stable and $\pi_1$-injective and satisfy a strict area--charge inequality.

papers.title: Teichm\"uller spaces with conical singularities and Virasoro coadjoint orbits
papers.abstract: We study Teichm\"uller spaces of hyperbolic \(0\)-metrics on a disk with ideal boundary and a marked point carrying a conical singularity with angle $\theta = 2\pi \beta$. For all $\beta>0$, we show that $\rm{Teich}^{\beta}(\overline{\mathbb D})\cong S^1\backslash \rm{Diff}(S^1)$, and we construct natural closed 2-forms $\omega_\beta$ induced by the Atiyah-Bott construction. For non-integer $\beta$, the form $\omega_\beta$ is symplectic, and one can identify $\rm{Teich}^{\beta}(\overline{\mathbb D})$ with the corresponding elliptic Virasoro coadjoint orbit. For positive integers $\beta=n$, $\omega_\beta$ is presymplectic, and it descends to the Kirillov-Kostant-Souriau symplectic form on the exceptional Virasoro orbit $\mathrm{PSU}^{(n)}(1,1)\backslash\rm{Diff}(S^1)$. Infinitesimal isometries of a hyperbolic \(0\)-metric on a disk with a conical singularity with angle $\theta=2\pi n$ are given by the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb R)$ which integrates to the group $\mathrm{PSU}^{(n)}(1,1)$ on the boundary of the disk but not in the interior for $n>1$. It is remarkable that the presymplectic structure of the corresponding Teichm\"uller spaces recovers this group and descends to the corresponding Virasoro coadjoint orbit.

papers.title: Elliptic Monotonicity Formulas for $p$-Green Functions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we derive $p$-Laplace analogues of Colding's three monotonicity formulas in the original metric on complete noncompact $n$-dimensional manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature, for $n\geq3$ and $1<p<n$. We assume a normalized positive minimal $p$-Green function vanishing at infinity with Euclidean pole asymptotics. Two complementary linearizations and the $p$-Bochner formula yield exact derivative identities with a common nonnegative defect involving an anisotropic trace-free Hessian and Ricci curvature. These identities give exterior cone rigidity and integral defect estimates, and recover the sharp gradient estimate and Euclidean rigidity of Mari--Rigoli--Setti. A one-parameter extension of Colding--Minicozzi type connects the formulas with known monotonicity and convexity identities for $p$-capacitary potentials.

papers.title: An intrinsic criterion for Pansu differentials to be homomorphisms of nilpotent Lie groups
papers.abstract: By Pansu's theorem, Lipschitz maps between Carnot groups are differentiable almost everywhere, and their differentials are group homomorphisms. When the domain is instead a nilpotent Lie group with a bracket-generating left-invariant distribution, the Pansu differential is a homomorphism of an osculating Carnot group, which depends on an auxiliary choice of grading, and it need not be a homomorphism of the original group. We give an intrinsic criterion for when it is one, for a suitable choice of grading: the differential must vanish on an ideal that depends only on the group and its distribution, and comes from a universal quotient onto a Carnot group. The criterion holds automatically when the step of the target is small enough, and an explicit example shows that this threshold is sharp. Along the way, we determine exactly how the obstruction depends on the choice of grading.

papers.title: Sharp Casorati Inequalities for Pointwise Bi-Slant Riemannian Maps into Sasakian Space Forms
papers.abstract: We establish Casorati inequalities for pointwise bi-slant Riemannian maps into Sasakian space forms with the characteristic vector field tangent to the range. The Sasakian structure imposes specific conditions on the second fundamental form, leading to refined inequalities for the normalized horizontal scalar curvature that also account for O'Neill's tensor. For proper pointwise bi-slant maps, equality in the two principal inequalities is characterized by the vanishing of the second fundamental form on the orthogonal complement of the characteristic direction in the range. We also derive corresponding inequalities for pointwise semi-slant, hemi-slant, and slant Riemannian maps and construct examples attaining equality.

papers.title: Curvature varifolds with given oriented boundary
papers.abstract: Let $\gamma\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a closed, embedded, connected, oriented $C^1$ submanifold in $\mathbb R^n$ of dimension $m-1$ where $2\leq m<n$. We prove that the area of any immersed $m$-dimensional submanifold with oriented boundary $\gamma$ is bounded in terms of its curvature energy, unless $\gamma$ lies in an $m$-plane. The problems leads to a weak formulation involving oriented curvature varifolds with given oriented boundary, and we solve a boundary-value minimization problem with obstacle in this class.

papers.title: DEC Fill-ins, the Bartnik--Bray inner mass, and positive mass theorems with untrapped boundary
papers.abstract: Given a closed $(n-1)$-dimensional manifold equipped with prescribed spacetime Bartnik data, we ask when this can be realised as the boundary of a compact $n$-dimensional initial data set satisfying the dominant energy condition (DEC). This is a natural generalisation of the problem of non-negative scalar curvature fill-ins, where the boundary metric and mean curvature are prescribed. We give conditions on the Bartnik data that suffice to prove the existence of such DEC fill-ins with inner MOTS boundary, and give some applications of these fill-ins. Our first application of these is a lower bound on the Bartnik--Bray inner mass, which we slightly reformulate here to be a genuine spacetime definition. Our other applications include proving a positive mass theorem for spin initial data with boundary that need not be trapped, and a spacetime Penrose-like inequality that gives a positive lower bound on the mass of an initial data set with boundary in terms of its boundary Bartnik data assuming the spacetime Penrose inequality holds.

papers.title: Energy and topology of Ricci-flat 4-manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that there is $C>0$ such that any complete Ricci-flat $4$-manifold $(M,g)$ satisfies $$ b_2(M)-C\leqslant\frac1{8\pi^2}\int_M|R_g|_g^2\,dv_g\leqslant b_2(M)+C, $$ where $R$ is the curvature operator. No assumption is made on volume growth, model at infinity or curvature decay. It follows that uncountably many exotic $\mathbb R^4$ admit no complete Ricci-flat metric, and that complete noncompact hyperk\"ahler metrics with finite $b_2$ have ends classified by Sun-Zhang. This also provides information about the thin part of immortal four-dimensional Ricci flows in Bamler's decomposition. The proof refines the chopping method of Cheeger-Gromov and Cheeger-Tian by bounding the topology of boundaries of regions exhausting the manifold.

papers.title: A Spectral Zoo of Genus-Zero Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces with Many Boundary Components
papers.abstract: We study critical points of the length-normalized first Steklov eigenvalue $\bar\sigma_1$ on genus-zero surfaces with $b$ boundary components. By a theorem of Fraser and Schoen, their first eigenfunctions give free boundary minimal surfaces in the unit ball. After uniformization, the domain is the round sphere minus $b$ round caps, with a weight on the boundary circles. A layer potential formulation gives the eigenvalues, their derivatives and a certificate for each critical point, and an exact multipole system for the caps. We compute a spectral zoo of 268 numerically certified critical points with up to $b=2252$ boundary components, including the $27$ embedded examples listed by Schulz. With their symmetry groups and Morse indices, the critical points satisfy a signed count for $3\le b\le10$. Most belong to families built from rings of boundary components. As the rings fill in, these appear to converge to the free curve minimal surfaces of Karpukhin and Noutchegueme, unions of flat disks and catenoidal annuli that meet along circles on the sphere. We construct these limits, among them the critical drum and the cake stand, a flat disk with a catenoidal horn. The families approach their limits like $j^{-1}$ for rings of $j$ caps, and the equatorial family approaches $4\pi$ with deficit $4\pi b^{-1}e^{-b}$. For large $b$, the leading terms of the multipole system reduce to the logarithmic energy of the cap centers and a formal evaluation gives $\bar\sigma_1^\star(b)=8\pi-16\pi\,b^{-1}\log b+O(b^{-1})$.

papers.title: Cup products with volume classes in bounded cohomology
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian $n$-manifold, $n\geq 2$, and suppose that either $M$ is negatively curved, or that it is a locally symmetric space of non-compact type. Via integration over straight simplices, every top-degree bounded differential form $\omega\in \Omega_b^n(M)$ defines a bounded cohomology class in $H^n_b(M)$. We prove that every such class belongs to the annihilator of the cup product in the whole graded algebra $H^{\geq 1}_b(M)$. In the case of closed orientable surfaces, this generalizes a result of Marasco, and, via transfer, provides a new proof of the fact that the cup product of the bounded Euler class of $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ with itself vanishes. Our result also applies to degree-3 bounded classes constructed by Soma and Farre, thus showing that, for surface groups and for free groups, the annihilator of the cup product is infinite dimensional also in degree 3.

papers.title: Quaternionic geometry of symplectic and contact pairs
papers.abstract: We introduce quaternionic analogues of symplectic pairs, contact--symplectic pairs and contact pairs. A hyper symplectic pair consists of three symplectic pairs whose sums form a positive quaternionic triple, while the contact analogues are defined through single or double symplectization. We prove that radial invariance of the induced complex structures is equivalent to the coincidence of the characteristic distributions, yielding a local product decomposition. Under a natural normalization, hyper contact--symplectic pairs are locally products of a $3$-Sasakian and a hyper-K\"ahler manifold and induce canonical $3$-quasi-Sasakian structures, whereas hyper contact pairs are locally products of two $3$-Sasakian manifolds. We construct compact examples for which these local decompositions are not global. Finally, compact normalized hyper contact pairs have finite fundamental group and are finite quotients of products of compact $3$-Sasakian manifolds, in contrast with normalized hyper contact--symplectic pairs, which may have infinite fundamental group.

papers.title: Dubrovin duality for open Hurwitz flat F-manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that the Dubrovin dual of a Hurwitz Frobenius manifold extends naturally to an F-manifold with compatible flat connection on the universal curve, in the sense of the open WDVV equations. A similar result is proven for the Frobenius manifold itself in arXiv:2503.09258 . This equips the universal curve with two F-manifolds with compatible flat structure, and we study their duality. We show that they combine into a bi-flat F-manifold. Conditions on open WDVV solutions imposed in previous work are retrieved in this setting, thus providing them with a geometrical meaning. Finally, explicit examples are computed. For Saito Frobenius manifolds of types $A$ and $D$, the extended prepotentials coincide with open WDVV solutions computed independently, whereas even the existence of the solution in type $E$ had not been previously discussed. On the other hand, new non-homogeneous solutions are constructed by duality.

papers.title: A question of Ulam and a theorem of de Rham
papers.abstract: We generalize de Rham's decomposition theorem to proper metric spaces: every proper metric space has a unique decomposition as the product of a Euclidean space and a finite or countable pointed $\ell^2$-product of nontrivial irreducible non-Euclidean factors. A slightly weaker unique decomposition statement is verified for general complete metric spaces. We use this to resolve a question of Ulam on the uniqueness of square roots of complete metric spaces.

papers.title: A Pogorelov-type estimate for the real twisted Monge-Amp\`ere equation
papers.abstract: We establish a Pogorelov type interior $C^2$ estimate for the real twisted Monge-Ampere equation without assuming uniform ellipticity. This equation is fully nonlinear and elliptic, but is neither concave nor a function of the eigenvalues of the Hessian, so the standard techniques for interior second-derivative estimates do not directly apply. Building on the partial Legendre transform formulation of Streets and Warren, we derive a differential identity for the associated positive-definite matrix $W(D^2u)$ and use some linear algebra to control the third-order terms arising in the maximum principle argument. As an application, we prove a Liouville theorem for entire split convex solutions with quadratic growth, extending the rigidity theorem of Streets and Warren by replacing their uniform ellipticity hypothesis with suitable quadratic growth assumptions.

papers.title: Area Rigidity for the Regular Representation of Surface Groups
papers.abstract: Let $\tilde{\Sigma}$ be the universal cover of a closed surface $\Sigma$ of genus at least $2$. We characterize all equivariantly area-minimizing maps from $\tilde{\Sigma}$ to a Hilbert sphere, which are equivariant with respect to an isometric action of $\pi_1(\Sigma)$ weakly equivalent to the regular representation. As part of our proof, we classify all totally isotropic minimal surfaces in Hilbert spheres with constant negative Gaussian curvature. This builds on earlier results of E. Calabi, K. Kenmotsu, R. Bryant.

papers.title: Timelike conjugate points in Lorentzian length spaces
papers.abstract: We study notions of conjugate points along timelike geodesics in the synthetic setting of Lorentzian (pre-)length spaces, inspired by earlier work for metric spaces by Shankar--Sormani. After preliminary considerations on convergence of timelike and causal geodesics, we introduce and compare one-sided, symmetric, unreachable and ultimate conjugate points along timelike geodesics. We show that all such notions are compatible with the usual one in the smooth (strongly causal) spacetime setting. As applications, we prove a timelike Rauch comparison theorem, as well as a result closely related to the recently established Lorentzian Cartan--Hadamard theorem by Er\"{o}s--Gieger. In the appendix, we give a detailed treatment of the Fr\'{e}chet distance on the space of non-stopping curves up to reparametrization, a technical tool used throughout the paper.

papers.title: From n-systems to Lie and Courant algebroids
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a method for constructing pure algebroids, dull algebroids, and Lie algebroids. The construction relies on what we call $n$-systems on vector bundles, and we provide explicit formulas for all resulting structure maps. Analogously, metric $n$-systems defined on metric vector bundles allow us to construct metric algebroids, pre-Courant algebroids, and Courant algebroids.
